function: CSI feedback with prediction: a Transformer encoder predicts future downlink geometric channel parameters from past channels; a Transformer decoder reconstructs the channel from quantized parameters (pp. 2, 5).
system: FDD MIMO-OFDM downlink: BS with 64 antennas, single-antenna UE, 1024 subcarriers, 100 MHz at 28 GHz; no RIS (pp. 2, 9-10).
method: Supervised Transformer encoder (multi-head self-attention) and decoder with 2D convolution, trained with NMSE losses; uniform quantizer; optimized bit allocation across AoD, delay, path loss, phase (pp. 5-9).
data_channel: Channels generated with the ray-tracing method of 3GPP TR 38.901 at 28 GHz; 80,000 training, 20,000 validation, 20,000 test samples; urban and rural variants (pp. 9, 11).
test_conditions: Split 80,000/20,000/20,000 samples; main runs at 3 km/h, also 60 and 108 km/h; urban and rural scenarios with testing on a scenario different from training (pp. 9, 11-12).
baselines: Non-learned: LASSO, DLRec (LS with angular-delay reciprocity); learned: CsiNet, TransNet, CVNN, Pruning, PTNet, CsiNet-LSTM; plus uniform-bit variant of the proposed method (pp. 9-11).
metrics: Channel NMSE (with and without quantization) versus SNR, feedback bits, timeslots and mobility; cosine similarity; BER with QPSK (pp. 10-12).
complexity: none; only feedback dimension and compression ratio (4L versus 2NfNt) are given, with no FLOPs, parameter count, or runtime (p. 5).
openness: none; no code or data link; channels generated with the 3GPP TR 38.901 ray-tracing method (p. 9).
q1_support: p. 9: "We generate the channel using the ray-tracing method described in 3GPP TR 38.901 [28]" - simulation built on 3GPP TR 38.901 (the system model of p. 3 is a generic geometric model).
q2_support: p. 12: "works well even when the tested scenario is different from the training scenario" - sentence starts at the end of p. 11, after the urban and rural experiment of Fig. 12; the training and test pairs are not detailed in the text.
q3_support: p. 9: "We compare the channel feedback performance of the proposed COMPaCT with eight baseline channel feedback techniques" - non-learned LASSO and DLRec; learned CsiNet, TransNet, CVNN, Pruning, PTNet, CsiNet-LSTM; compared on NMSE (Figs. 6-8, 11).
q4_support: p. 5: "Note that the compression ratio of the proposed COMPaCT is" - feedback dimension only (4L versus 2NfNt); no FLOPs, parameters or runtime of the Transformer is reported; the 8855 brute-force combinations (p. 8) belong to the bit-allocation search that the closed form avoids.
q5_support: p. 9: "We generate the channel using the ray-tracing method described in 3GPP TR 38.901 [28]" - data generated by the authors; no code or data link, no public dataset and no measured data.
notes: PDF is the arXiv v1 preprint (2410.06504v1, 9 Oct 2024; p. 1). Area 2: CSI feedback and channel prediction. The UE has one antenna but the BS has 64 (p. 9), so the single-antenna exclusion does not apply. q2 rests on one sentence about cross-scenario testing (urban versus rural, Fig. 12, pp. 11-12); the exact training and test pairs are not described in the text.
